College Park share of Port Moody listings and sales by month

In College Park, its share of the houses listed in Port Moody went from 9.4% in June to 10.4% in September and its share of the condos and townhomes listed went from 11.6% to 9.4%. A share that holds steady while the city moves means the community is following the city; a share that drifts means it is moving differently.

blocks.text: College Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

27 townhomes sold in College Park with a median price of $829,000 (the middle half sold between $765,000 and $883,500), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 98.4% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $485 per square foot, a median year built of 1977 and a median strata fee of $626 a month. 16 houses sold in College Park with a median price of $1,640,850 (the middle half sold between $1,353,750 and $1,858,750), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 19% sold above list. They had a median $600 per square foot, a median year built of 1973 and a median lot of 7,594 square feet.

Fee-simple lots — the default form: detached homes here are freehold; a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. The attached stock is strata titled — built strata stock, not land.

Hazards and buildable area: the OCP provides environmentally sensitive area and hazardous lands / steep slope development permit areas (DPA 4 and DPA 5), and watercourse lots need riparian assessment under Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 — that diligence decides how much of a lot is actually buildable. No floodplain or ALR land was confirmed in College Park.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around College Park PM

items.t: College Park is an established residential area at Port Moody's west end, next to Glenayre and Seaview near the Burnaby border, in the Clarke Road / Barnet Highway side of the city south of the inlet. The City's OCP material names College Park among the city's older single detached areas. Exact board sub-area boundary roads are UNVERIFIED.

Nearby areas: Glenayre and Seaview next door, Port Moody Centre to the east, Burnaby (Burnaby Mountain / SFU side) to the west. Barnet Highway (Highway 7A) and St. Johns Street run east–west through the city toward Burnaby and Coquitlam. Driving commute times: UNVERIFIED.

Transit: TransLink buses connect west Port Moody to Moody Centre Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express); Moody Centre and Inlet Centre are the city's two SkyTrain stops, east of this area. Specific route numbers on College Park streets are UNVERIFIED.

Community Port Moody (medians are published at community level only; sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED): detached median $1,685,000, $608/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 33 days; condos & townhomes median $715,000, $666/sq ft, 94%, 29 days. Land has NO SnapStats category — no figure above is a land figure.

Schools (SD43 Coquitlam, Ministry-listed names): SD43 schools in this part of Port Moody include Glenayre Elementary and Seaview Community School, with Moody Middle and Port Moody Secondary serving central Port Moody. The status of the College Park Elementary school building (300 Princeton Avenue) is UNVERIFIED on an SD43 source — it does not appear in the district's current Port Moody school list used for this research.

Recreation: Glenayre Centre at 492 Glencoe Drive is the City community centre in the adjoining Glenayre neighbourhood, and the Port Moody Recreation Complex is at 300 Ioco Road; Port Moody Public Library is at 100 Newport Drive. Parks inside College Park itself: UNVERIFIED on an official source. Rocky Point Park and the Shoreline Trail at the head of the inlet are the city's waterfront park system east of this area.
Health: Eagle Ridge Hospital is in Port Moody at 475 Guildford Way (Fraser Health), east of this area.
Shopping: no shopping centre or grocery store location inside College Park was verified on an official source: UNVERIFIED.
How people search for it: "College Park Port Moody," "College Park PM." No other official alternate name was confirmed: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in College Park PM

items.t: OCP — Port Moody Official Community Plan Bylaw 2026 No. 3522 (adopted Apr 28, 2026, repeals Bylaw No. 2955 — never cite 2955 as current): Its Chapter 14 sets policy for the city's neighbourhoods; the Suncor refinery lands beside College Park and Seaview are designated a Special Study Area, which is the main planning item hanging over this end of the city.

Zoning — Port Moody Zoning Bylaw No. 2937: single detached homes in RS zones and multi-residential homes in RT and RM zones; small-scale multi-unit housing is permitted in RS and RT zones outside the transit-oriented areas. Any parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, UNVERIFIED.

SSMUH / small-lot position — Port Moody, as the City states it: small-scale multi-unit housing, including coach houses and accessory dwelling units, is permitted in RS and RT zones outside the transit-oriented areas; the transit-oriented areas are exempt from the SSMUH rules. Small lots: RS1-S small lot subdivision (minimum 9 m width and 325 m²) is available only in Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside OCP Single Family–Low Density areas — College Park is not on that list, so confirm any lot-split idea with the City before relying on it.
Subdivision and servicing — Port Moody: no verified bylaw number exists, held UNCONFIRMED

Riparian / slope diligence: watercourse lots need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks, and environmentally sensitive (DPA 4) and steep-slope (DPA 5) development permit areas can apply. Whether a specific lot is in a permit area: UNVERIFIED per parcel.

Property taxes — City of Port Moody: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding amounts after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; utilities are billed separately, with the 2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026.

ALR block (carried for completeness — no ALR land was confirmed in College Park): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check a parcel on the ALC maps.

blocks.text: Good to know about College Park PM

items.t: Port Moody replaced its OCP in 2026 (Apr 28, 2026). Bylaw 2026 No. 3522 repeals No. 2955 — packages still citing 2955 as the current OCP are out of date, and the change is less than a year old at this research date.
The namesake school may not be a school anymore (Nov 1, 2026).

Two Clarke Road addresses, two tenures (Nov 2, 2026). Clarke Townhomes at 909 Clarke Road is a counted strata complex; Mountain View Housing Co-operative at 902 Clarke Road is co-op tenure, excluded everywhere — a feed that sorts by street alone can merge them.

The refinery lands next door are an open question, not a plan (Nov 1, 2026). The Suncor lands' Special Study Area designation means no approved future use exists to price — buyers asking what will be built there are asking about a study, not a project: project details UNVERIFIED.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in College Park?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 14 houses and 18 condos and townhomes listed in College Park. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is College Park a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 14% (a balanced market); condos and townhomes had 22% (a sellers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in College Park from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 7 houses and 16 condos and townhomes sold in College Park over those 4 months; detached houses peaked in July with 5 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 4 sold.

faq.q: How big is College Park compared with the rest of Port Moody?
faq.a: In September 2026, College Park held 10.4% of the 135 detached houses listed in Port Moody and 9.4% of the 192 condos and townhomes listed in Port Moody.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in College Park?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses made up 43.8% of the 32 homes listed in College Park and condos and townhomes made up 56.2%; of the 6 that sold, houses were 33.3% and condos and townhomes 66.7%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in College Park than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses rose from 12 in June to 14 in September 2026 (+16.7%); condos and townhomes fell from 25 in June to 18 in September 2026 (−28.0%).

faq.q: What did townhomes in College Park sell for?
faq.a: 27 townhomes sold in College Park between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $829,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in College Park?
faq.a: The median was 26 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 98.4% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Can a College Park lot be split into small lots?
faq.a: Not under the RS1-S small lot rule as published — that subdivision option (minimum 9 m width and 325 m²) is limited to Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside OCP Single Family–Low Density areas, and College Park is not on the list, so confirm any subdivision idea with the City before pricing in subdivision value.

faq.q: Which OCP governs a College Park lot?
faq.a: OCP Bylaw 2026 No. 3522, adopted April 28, 2026, which repeals Bylaw No. 2955 — any package still citing 2955 as current is out of date.

faq.q: Can I add a coach house or suites to a College Park lot under SSMUH?
faq.a: Small-scale multi-unit housing, including coach houses and accessory dwelling units, is permitted on qualifying RS and RT lots outside the transit-oriented areas — College Park is outside the station areas, so the frame can apply per-lot; confirm the specific lot with the City.

faq.q: How did College Park trade in September 2026?
faq.a: As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

faq.q: What extra diligence does a creek or slope lot need?
faq.a: A riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks for watercourse lots, plus any environmentally sensitive (DPA 4) or steep-slope (DPA 5) development permit area that applies — that diligence decides the buildable area, not the lot's gross size.
